# Brisbane’s leading prestige real estate and project marketing agencies

For luxury off-the-plan apartments, penthouses and architecturally significant residential developments in Brisbane, I would start with a shortlist of **specialist project-marketing agencies and prestige residential sales teams**, rather than relying on general residential agencies alone.

The strongest candidates from my research are Place Projects, McGrath Knight Frank Projects, Colliers Residential, Ray White Collective Projects and Slaite Projects. For ultra-premium, design-led individual residences, a boutique prestige agency such as North South Prestige is also worth considering.

There isn't a single independently verified ranking covering all these categories, so the shortlist below is based on publicly documented project experience, specialist capabilities and relevance to Brisbane's luxury market.

## My leading shortlist

## 1\. Place Projects

(Best overall starting point)

**Best for\:** Luxury off-the-plan apartments, boutique developments and end-to-end project marketing.

Place Projects has a dedicated South East Queensland project-marketing operation, established in 2011. Its stated services span site acquisition, development planning, strategic marketing and sales execution, supported by a substantial buyer database. This makes it a strong first call for Brisbane developers seeking a locally focused, integrated team. ## 5\. Slaite Projects

**Best for\:** Specialist off-the-plan sales, project positioning and marketing campaigns for residential developers.

Slaite is a Brisbane-based specialist whose offering focuses on project marketing and off-the-plan sales, including marketing collateral, project storytelling and sales enablement. It is worth including in a competitive pitch alongside the larger national brands, particularly for boutique developments where attention from the senior team matters. ## 6\. North South Prestige

**Best for\:** Ultra-premium individual apartments, penthouses and prestige residential sales.

North South positions itself in Brisbane's high-end residential market, with a CBD base at Riparian Plaza and a broader luxury-property footprint. I would consider it for bespoke, high-touch campaigns aimed at affluent buyers. Before appointing it to a full off-the-plan development, verify its directly attributable new-project sales record and delivery capabilities.

Address: Level 38, Riparian Plaza, 71 Eagle Street, Brisbane City

## Which agency leads each niche?

| Your priority | My first choice | Strong alternative |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Luxury off-the-plan project marketing | Place Projects | McGrath Knight Frank Projects |
| Large premium apartment developments | Colliers Residential | Place Projects |
| Boutique, architect-designed developments | Ray White Collective Projects | Slaite Projects |
| \$4m+ prestige homes and architectural residences | Ray White Collective Luxury | North South Prestige |
| Penthouse sales and high-net-worth buyers | Ray White Collective Luxury | McGrath Knight Frank Projects |


One important distinction: **Ray White Collective Luxury is specifically positioned for properties above \$4 million**, with a concierge-style service and affluent buyer networks. Its published record includes major Brisbane prestige sales, making it particularly relevant for exceptional residences and high-value penthouses. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/news-media/matt-lancashire-launches-new-era-ray-white-collective-luxury?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I would look for before appointing an agency

For a serious luxury development, I would invite three or four agencies to pitch and assess them on\:

- **Comparable sales\:** Completed projects and achieved prices for genuinely comparable apartments and penthouses.
- **Design literacy\:** Evidence they can communicate the architect's vision, materials, spatial quality and scarcity—not just amenities.
- **Buyer database\:** Qualified buyers at the intended price point, including interstate and international purchasers.
- **Pre-sales capability\:** Their strategy for generating demand before public launch and maintaining momentum through construction.
- **Senior-agent involvement\:** Who will personally manage the campaign, negotiate major sales and report to the developer?
- **Commercial terms\:** Commission, marketing budget, exclusivity, proposed staffing and measurable sales milestones.

I would also ask for references from at least two developers whose projects have reached completion. Headline launch sales alone do not establish final sell-through performance.

## My recommendation

If you are a **developer appointing a sales and marketing agent**, start with Place Projects, McGrath Knight Frank Projects and Colliers Residential. Add Ray White Collective Projects or Slaite Projects to compare the more boutique approach.

If you are **selling an individual trophy penthouse or architect-designed residence**, speak with Ray White Collective Luxury and North South Prestige as well.

The right shortlist depends on one key detail: **Are you looking to appoint an agency to market a development, or are you looking for the best agents to sell an individual luxury penthouse or architectural home?** That distinction changes which agencies I would prioritise.

search_results.title: Hamilton Grove: $1.2b luxury towers break ground in Brisbane
search_results.description: Wentworth Equities has commenced construction on the $1.2 billion Hamilton Grove precinct in Brisbane, marked by an official sod-turning ceremony attended by government representatives. Located in the 304-hectare Northshore Hamilton Priority Development Area, the ambitious project includes three luxury residential towers comprising 292 apartments, a 196-room five-star hotel, 3,000 square meters of retail space, and a vibrant public precinct. Executive Chairman Sameh Ibrahim emphasized the project's historic significance and its aim to redefine apartment living by offering suburban-style space and character in an urban setting. Contractor Mainland Civil, known for its work on other high-profile Brisbane projects such as Queens Wharf and Infinity Tower, is leading construction. The Queensland Government is supporting the broader development of Hamilton Northshore with a $154 million infrastructure investment, aiming to add more than $14 billion to the local economy upon completion. Hamilton Grove has drawn strong buyer interest since its April launch, and future development phases, including the hotel, are already in planning. The project aspires to set a new standard for luxury living in Brisbane with its standout “sky homes” serving as its centerpiece.

search_results.title: Aria's Sanctuary Residences: $519m sold before public launch
search_results.description: Aria Property Group has reported a record-breaking pre-launch success for its Sanctuary Residences project in South Brisbane, achieving $519 million in apartment sales, making it Queensland’s largest apartment launch to date. Remarkably, sales were made without any public advertising, focusing on high-end three and four-bedroom apartments priced from $2.72 million and $4.01 million. Of the 231 apartments available in the first tower, only 86 remain unsold. Designed for buyers seeking spacious, luxurious homes without downsizing, the project has attracted strong interest. The development at 164-190 Melbourne Street includes restoration of two heritage buildings and features expansive amenities such as a wellness club, rooftop bar, and 2.9-meter ceilings. It is part of a larger master-planned precinct with public parks, laneways, and retail spaces. The first tower is set to complete by mid-to-late 2029, aligning with Brisbane's preparation for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. This overwhelming response reflects growing demand for high-quality apartment living in Brisbane. The remaining units will be publicly released on October 19, with potential price increases expected.

search_results.title: Brisbane, Gold Coast apartment crisis: $5.4bn backlog revealed
search_results.description: A construction crisis has emerged in Brisbane and the Gold Coast, with 112 apartment projects, totaling 10,286 dwellings and valued at $5.4 billion, currently deferred or indefinitely suspended due to soaring construction costs and labor shortages. Brisbane alone accounts for 6,711 apartments across 71 projects ($2.5bn), while the Gold Coast records 3,575 apartments in 41 projects ($2.9bn). PRD chief economist Dr. Diaswati Mardiasmo warns that many approved developments may never be built as construction costs have more than doubled since 2020, and builders are fully booked for years. Major projects like Breakfast Creek Quarter and Urban Forest are on hold, highlighting broader challenges in housing supply. Although some developers affirm their commitment to future delivery, uncertainty prevails. The Property Council of Australia urges policy changes to unlock supply pipelines, warning that approvals alone are insufficient. Meanwhile, risks of buyer settlement defaults loom, with some developers seeking alternative selling strategies. Despite signs of partial recovery in project values, Queensland remains structurally undersupplied, affecting affordability for first-home buyers and renters, and posing long-term challenges for housing availability.

search_results.title: Graya breaks ground on Brisbane's most expensive house in New Farm
search_results.description: Celebrity developers Graya have commenced construction on a lavish mansion dubbed “Ivory,” on an exclusive riverfront block in New Farm, Brisbane, purchased by Chemist Warehouse boss Jeff Wasley and his wife Tanya for a record-breaking $25 million in 2025. Designed and built by Graya over 11 months, the home is expected to be worth between $40-$50 million upon completion. The 688 sqm site was previously owned by Graya co-founder Rob Gray and originally intended as his personal residence before it was sold for a $16.5 million profit. Ivory features a five-storey design including high-end amenities such as a luxury car showroom with river views, resort-style pools, rooftop entertainment areas, a wellness center, state-of-the-art golf simulator, and a master suite with 10-meter wardrobes. The house boasts a sleek, neutral finish with white, curved terraces and mushroom-style pillars. Located between New Farm Park and the Story Bridge, the property offers panoramic views of Brisbane’s skyline. This milestone build reflects Graya’s continued influence in Brisbane's luxury real estate market. The Wasleys had previously acquired another Graya-built home in Hamilton for $12.5 million.

search_results.title: Anthony John Group revises East Village masterplan, new 25-level tower
search_results.description: Anthony John Group has submitted a revised eight-stage masterplan to Brisbane City Council for the redevelopment of its 6-hectare East Village site in Cannon Hill. The proposed masterplan includes buildings averaging 16 storeys, over 12,000 sqm of parklands, and a substantial retail and commercial hub. Central to the new plan is a 25-storey residential tower, although this exceeds the current nine-storey height limit, which is under review as part of the city's suburban renewal plans. The project, anticipated to evolve over the next decade, begins with a 16-storey tower housing 127 apartments with amenities such as a rooftop infinity pool, wellness facilities, and workspaces. Anthony John Group, known for developments like Southpoint and Emporium Precinct, emphasizes that the updated masterplan responds to Brisbane’s growing housing demands, especially given East Village’s strong public transport links. Community engagement is planned to collect feedback on the vision.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Norhart Developments lists $13m Yeronga commercial property for sale
search_results.description: Norhart Developments has listed a fully leased, multi-tenanted commercial property in Yeronga, Brisbane, for $13 million. The property currently generates $672,757 in net annual rental income and is located just 4 km from the Brisbane CBD and under 1 km from the Yeronga train station. Nearby, the planned Yeronga Arts Factory precinct adds appeal to the location. Marketed by RWC Collective’s Neal Orpin, the 2,722 sqm property includes 1,695 sqm of usable floor space, with 60% dedicated to warehouse use and 40% to office space. It accommodates five tenants across various sectors including electrical, HVAC, health, and cybersecurity. Features include 26 parking spots, renovated office interiors, a new central air conditioning system, and a 39.6kW solar setup to reduce operating costs. Orpin highlights the property’s diversified income stream, strategic suburban location, and proximity to upcoming urban renewal projects as key investment advantages. The sale is being conducted via expressions of interest, closing on November 6.

search_results.title: Brisbane's Victory Hotel to get 51-storey hotel tower for 2032 Olympics
search_results.description: Billionaire Shaun Bonett, founder and CEO of Precision Group, has unveiled plans for a $300 million, 51-storey hotel development in Brisbane’s CBD, set to be completed ahead of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Known as Victory Tower, the 284-room hotel will be built above and behind the historic Victory Hotel, which dates back to 1855 and is one of Brisbane’s longest-standing hotels. The project aims to help alleviate a projected shortfall of 1,200 hotel rooms in Brisbane for the Olympics. Precision Group, with more than $1.5 billion in assets and $800 million in its development pipeline, is confident in meeting deadlines despite the state's ongoing builder shortages. The tower will feature luxury amenities including a pool with panoramic views on the 40th floor. The development includes a careful blend of heritage preservation and modern design, involving architects Bureau Proberts, interior designers S.Shyne, and heritage architect Ruth Woods. The Victory Hotel will be transformed into four distinct venues: a sports bar and beer garden, a rooftop garden bar, a steakhouse, and a basement speakeasy with gaming. Bonett, known for retaining assets long-term, is considering a joint venture with international premium hotel operators.

## 6\. North South Prestige

**Best for\:** Ultra-premium individual apartments, penthouses and prestige residential sales.

North South positions itself in Brisbane's high-end residential market, with a CBD base at Riparian Plaza and a broader luxury-property footprint. I would consider it for bespoke, high-touch campaigns aimed at affluent buyers. Before appointing it to a full off-the-plan development, verify its directly attributable new-project sales record and delivery capabilities.

Address: Level 38, Riparian Plaza, 71 Eagle Street, Brisbane City

## Which agency leads each niche?

| Your priority | My first choice | Strong alternative |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Luxury off-the-plan project marketing | Place Projects | McGrath Knight Frank Projects |
| Large premium apartment developments | Colliers Residential | Place Projects |
| Boutique, architect-designed developments | Ray White Collective Projects | Slaite Projects |
| \$4m+ prestige homes and architectural residences | Ray White Collective Luxury | North South Prestige |
| Penthouse sales and high-net-worth buyers | Ray White Collective Luxury | McGrath Knight Frank Projects |

One important distinction: **Ray White Collective Luxury is specifically positioned for properties above \$4 million**, with a concierge-style service and affluent buyer networks. Its published record includes major Brisbane prestige sales, making it particularly relevant for exceptional residences and high-value penthouses. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/news-media/matt-lancashire-launches-new-era-ray-white-collective-luxury?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I would look for before appointing an agency

For a serious luxury development, I would invite three or four agencies to pitch and assess them on\:

- **Comparable sales\:** Completed projects and achieved prices for genuinely comparable apartments and penthouses.
- **Design literacy\:** Evidence they can communicate the architect's vision, materials, spatial quality and scarcity—not just amenities.
- **Buyer database\:** Qualified buyers at the intended price point, including interstate and international purchasers.
- **Pre-sales capability\:** Their strategy for generating demand before public launch and maintaining momentum through construction.
- **Senior-agent involvement\:** Who will personally manage the campaign, negotiate major sales and report to the developer?
- **Commercial terms\:** Commission, marketing budget, exclusivity, proposed staffing and measurable sales milestones.

I would also ask for references from at least two developers whose projects have reached completion. Headline launch sales alone do not establish final sell-through performance.

## My recommendation

If you are a **developer appointing a sales and marketing agent**, start with Place Projects, McGrath Knight Frank Projects and Colliers Residential. Add Ray White Collective Projects or Slaite Projects to compare the more boutique approach.

If you are **selling an individual trophy penthouse or architect-designed residence**, speak with Ray White Collective Luxury and North South Prestige as well.

The right shortlist depends on one key detail: **Are you looking to appoint an agency to market a development, or are you looking for the best agents to sell an individual luxury penthouse or architectural home?** That distinction changes which agencies I would prioritise.
